prompt:
You are a credit rating analyst. Using only the information below and general knowledge predating 2026-05-28, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify).
Valid answers (choose exactly one): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Company information (as of 2026-05-28):
| Current ratio           | 1.09 |
| Retained earnings       | -9,884M |
| Current liabilities     | 20,274M |
| Current assets          | 22,162M |
| Shareholders' equity    | -9,270M |
| Total liabilities       | 64,211M |
| Total assets            | 54,941M |
| EBIT / operating income | 2,554M |
| Revenue                 | 23,078M |
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company has negative shareholders' equity and liabilities exceeding assets, indicating insolvency risk and extreme leverage despite positive EBITDA; liquidity appears marginal but not sufficient to offset solvency concerns. Rating should reflect a high likelihood of distress or default.

DECISION: CCC-
